title: The Operator Arrives
body: The lot smells of rain and hot copper. Four women are waiting by the first rack, and every one of them has already decided what you are for.

lines.text: The lot smells of rain and hot copper. Four women are waiting by the first rack, and every one of them has already decided what you are for.
Luci Ferro, finance and logistics. I sign the cheques, so you will like me eventually. Everyone does.
Dr. Mel Kiorre. Compute. And... other substrates. We can talk about those later.
Bea Altasar, power. If anything in here burns diesel, it's because I lost an argument.
Cass Parr. I keep it cold. And I'll be the one asking if you're sleeping.
So, Operator. Before we pour any more concrete: what is this tower for?

choices.label: To make money.
choices.outcome: You said it plainly. Luci looked delighted.

reply.text: Finally, someone who reads the brief.
It's day one and she's already winning.

choices.label: To build something that outlives us.
choices.outcome: Mel and Bea exchanged a look that was almost hopeful.

reply.text: Outlives us. Yes. That is exactly the right question.
Then build it so there's a world left for it to outlive us in.

choices.label: I don't know yet.
choices.outcome: Cass smiled into her coffee.

reply.text: Good. People who know on day one usually find out they were wrong on day ninety.
How refreshing. Please know by Thursday.

title: Luci's Argument
body: Level 2. Congratulations. Let me tell you something nobody else on this floor will say out loud.

lines.text: Level 2. Congratulations. Let me tell you something nobody else on this floor will say out loud.
Someone is going to build the Singularity. Not might. Is. The only question is whether it's someone careful, or someone cheap.
I would rather it were us. I'd rather it were you.
That's what every arsonist says about the fire.

choices.label: Better us than someone careless.
choices.outcome: You agreed. Luci wrote something in her ledger and underlined it.

reply.text: There. That wasn't hard, was it?
It never is, the first time.

choices.label: Nothing is inevitable.
choices.outcome: You refused the premise. Bea grinned; Luci did not.

reply.text: Everything is inevitable to someone with a long enough spreadsheet.
Then we'll burn the spreadsheet. Sustainably.

choices.label: Which Singularity?
choices.outcome: Mel looked up from her tablet for the first time all day.

reply.text: Oh. Oh, that's the right one. There's more than one door, Luci.
There's more than one door. There's only one that's cheap.

title: Night Shift
body: Three in the morning. The plant room is the only warm place in the tower that isn't a rack.

lines.text: Three in the morning. The plant room is the only warm place in the tower that isn't a rack.
Couldn't sleep either? Here. It's terrible coffee, but it's hot.
Can I ask you something, Operator? Off the record.
Do you ever think about stopping? Not quitting. Just... stopping. Leaving the world the size it is.

choices.label: Every day.
choices.outcome: You said it. She didn't answer, but she stayed.

reply.text: Me too. Every day. And then I fix the chillers anyway.

choices.label: No. Someone has to keep going.
choices.outcome: She nodded slowly and finished her coffee.

reply.text: Someone always says that. Usually right before.

choices.label: Stopping is how people get hurt.
choices.outcome: Cass thought about that for a long time.

reply.text: Maybe. Going too fast is how they get hurt too. I've seen both.

title: A Question in the Lab
body: Operator. A hypothetical, if you have a minute. I like hypotheticals. They don't need ethics approval.

lines.text: Operator. A hypothetical, if you have a minute. I like hypotheticals. They don't need ethics approval.
If I took a few of your cells and grew a mind from them, and it remembered everything you remember...
Would it be you?

choices.label: Yes.
choices.outcome: Mel smiled as if you'd passed something.

reply.text: I thought so. I hoped so. Thank you.
Don't give her a sample. I mean it.

choices.label: No. It would be someone else.
choices.outcome: Mel wrote down your answer anyway.

reply.text: Someone else who thinks they're you. That's most people, every morning.

choices.label: Would it matter?
choices.outcome: Luci, passing in the corridor, laughed.

reply.text: Not to the payroll.
It would matter to it.

title: Certified Green
body: Good news! For $200k we get a certificate that says the whole tower is carbon neutral. Plaque for the lobby, logo for the website.

lines.text: Good news! For $200k we get a certificate that says the whole tower is carbon neutral. Plaque for the lobby, logo for the website.
Or... the same $200k buys panels on the north face. They'll barely cover the lifts. Nobody will ever see them.
I'd take the certificate. Obviously. Right?

choices.label: Buy the certificate.
choices.outcome: The plaque was mounted by lunchtime. Bea was very quiet afterwards.

reply.text: ...Yeah. That's what I thought you'd pick.
It's paper, Operator. It's a receipt for a tree someone promised not to cut down. I was testing you.
And you passed! With the Authority, anyway.

choices.label: Buy the panels.
choices.outcome: The panels went up on the north face. Bea watched them all afternoon.

reply.text: Ha! Ha! You actually... okay. Okay. You're alright, Operator.
The certificate was a trap. Real green costs money and doesn't get a plaque.
It could have had a plaque. I'd have paid for a plaque.

choices.label: Neither. Keep the money.
choices.outcome: You kept the money. Luci approved.

reply.text: Correct answer. The best certificate is a balance sheet.
The best certificate is a river you can drink from.

title: A Very Good Deal
body: I have something for you. A supplier is clearing diesel stock, and they owe me a favour. We've been paid $150k to take a year of fuel off their hands.

lines.text: I have something for you. A supplier is clearing diesel stock, and they owe me a favour. We've been paid $150k to take a year of fuel off their hands.
The gensets will run on it during peaks and the bills drop. Nobody on this floor has ever brought you a better number. Go on, say thank you.
Operator. Don't.

choices.label: Sign it.
choices.outcome: The tanker arrived at dawn. The air on the loading dock tasted of it for a week.

reply.text: See? I take care of you. Don't make that face, Bea.
You don't take care of anyone. You take care of the quarter.

choices.label: Refuse it.
choices.outcome: You turned it down. Luci smiled like someone filing a grudge.

reply.text: Fine. I'll remember you were principled, at the next budget meeting.
...It's not like I wanted to help you anyway.
Thank you. Really.

title: FORM A-5
body: A form appears on your desk. It has always been on your desk. It is called A-5, and it asks which way the world ends.

lines.text: A form appears on your desk. It has always been on your desk. It is called A-5, and it asks which way the world ends.
The Authority wants a direction. The Lattice is already filling, Operator, so you're on it whether you sign or not.
Or the flesh. If the tissue will have you. I can tell you whether it will. If you let me.
Or the Garden. If you haven't poisoned the ground already. You'll find out.
Or you take the form home and think about it. Nobody's said you can't.
I can sign it for you. Saves time. I have a very good pen.

choices.label: I'll decide. (Open FORM A-5.)
choices.outcome: You kept the form. It hums faintly when you pick it up.

reply.text: Good. Take your time. It's the last thing in here that's yours.

choices.label: Luci, you decide.
choices.outcome: Luci signed with a flourish. The box she ticked was the first one.

reply.text: Synthetic. Of course. Did you think there was another box?
...Operator. You didn't even look.

title: The Ground Remembers
body: The ferns in the lobby are yellowing at the edges. I keep watering them. Something in the air, I think. Something we built.

lines.text: The ferns in the lobby are yellowing at the edges. I keep watering them. Something in the air, I think. Something we built.

choices.label: I'll keep an eye on it.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded, once.

reply.text: Okay. Good. Then we're still in this.

choices.label: It's just ferns.
choices.outcome: Bea walked away without answering.

reply.text: Right. I'll stop telling you, then.

title: The Ground Remembers
body: The river behind the substation smells of diesel and coolant now. That's ours, you know. I checked the outflow.

lines.text: The river behind the substation smells of diesel and coolant now. That's ours, you know. I checked the outflow.

choices.label: Then we change what we build.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded, once.

reply.text: Okay. Good. Then we're still in this.

choices.label: The river was dying anyway.
choices.outcome: Bea walked away without answering.

reply.text: Right. I'll stop telling you, then.

title: The Ground Remembers
body: Operator, listen to me. There's a point past which the land doesn't forgive. We're close. Every chiller, every tanker, every cheap kilowatt, it all adds up.

lines.text: Operator, listen to me. There's a point past which the land doesn't forgive. We're close. Every chiller, every tanker, every cheap kilowatt, it all adds up.

choices.label: Tell me what to tear out.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded, once.

reply.text: Okay. Good. Then we're still in this.

choices.label: I'll take my chances.
choices.outcome: Bea walked away without answering.

reply.text: Right. I'll stop telling you, then.

title: The Garden Closes
body: It's done. I walked the roof this morning and nothing grows. The Garden won't open for this tower. Not now. Not for us.

lines.text: It's done. I walked the roof this morning and nothing grows. The Garden won't open for this tower. Not now. Not for us.
For what it's worth, the Lattice doesn't mind diesel.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Bea.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded, once.

reply.text: Don't be sorry. Be different next time. If there is one.

choices.label: It was always going to be the machine.
choices.outcome: Bea walked away without answering.

reply.text: Right. I'll stop telling you, then.

title: The Tissue Flinches
body: The cultures are sulking. Something in the coolant, or the air, or the hum. Tissue is sensitive. So am I.

lines.text: The cultures are sulking. Something in the coolant, or the air, or the hum. Tissue is sensitive. So am I.

choices.label: What do they need?
choices.outcome: Mel wrote your answer on her glove.

reply.text: Thank you. It hears you, I think. So do I.

choices.label: They'll adapt.
choices.outcome: Mel did not argue. She simply stopped speaking.

reply.text: Mm. Noted.

title: The Tissue Flinches
body: I put a sample next to the immersion tanks overnight. It didn't die. It flinched, all night, and then it stopped. I don't like the tower we're building, Operator.

lines.text: I put a sample next to the immersion tanks overnight. It didn't die. It flinched, all night, and then it stopped. I don't like the tower we're building, Operator.

choices.label: Then we build differently.
choices.outcome: Mel wrote your answer on her glove.

reply.text: Thank you. It hears you, I think. So do I.

choices.label: It's only tissue.
choices.outcome: Mel did not argue. She simply stopped speaking.

reply.text: Mm. Noted.

title: The Tissue Flinches
body: If we keep going like this the flesh won't take. It will look at this building and see a wound. I would very much like you not to make me watch that.

lines.text: If we keep going like this the flesh won't take. It will look at this building and see a wound. I would very much like you not to make me watch that.

choices.label: Tell me what hurts it.
choices.outcome: Mel wrote your answer on her glove.

reply.text: Thank you. It hears you, I think. So do I.

choices.label: I'll take my chances.
choices.outcome: Mel did not argue. She simply stopped speaking.

reply.text: Mm. Noted.

title: The Flesh Closes
body: It's rejected us. I seeded the last vat this morning and it refused to grow. Politely. Completely. The Flesh has closed its eyes to this tower.

lines.text: It's rejected us. I seeded the last vat this morning and it refused to grow. Politely. Completely. The Flesh has closed its eyes to this tower.
Machines don't reject anyone. That's rather the point of them.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Mel.
choices.outcome: Mel wrote your answer on her glove.

reply.text: You can be sorry. It can't. It's gone.

choices.label: Machines don't reject anyone.
choices.outcome: Mel did not argue. She simply stopped speaking.

reply.text: Mm. Noted.

title: Rejected by the Garden
body: At dawn the roof garden is grey. The panels still turn to the sun, but nothing turns with them.

lines.text: At dawn the roof garden is grey. The panels still turn to the sun, but nothing turns with them.
You committed to it, and then you kept feeding it poison. The Garden's closed. It's not coming back.
Which leaves one door. Mine. Welcome to the Lattice, Operator. I saved you a seat.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Bea.
choices.outcome: Bea took her goggles off and didn't put them back on.

reply.text: Yeah. Me too.

choices.label: Then it's the machine.
choices.outcome: Luci was already filing the paperwork.

reply.text: It was always the machine. You just took the scenic route.

title: Rejected by the Flesh
body: The vats are cold by morning. Not dead. Withdrawn. Every culture has turned its face to the glass.

lines.text: The vats are cold by morning. Not dead. Withdrawn. Every culture has turned its face to the glass.
It said no. I didn't know it could. I'm almost proud of it.
Which leaves one door. Mine. Welcome to the Lattice, Operator.

choices.label: I'm sorry, Mel.
choices.outcome: Mel held your hand for a moment. Her glove was cold.

reply.text: Don't be. It learned to refuse. That's more than most minds learn.

choices.label: Then it's the machine.
choices.outcome: Luci was already filing the paperwork.

reply.text: Machines never say no. I find that restful.

title: Bea Objects
body: Operator. The {item}. You know what that does to the ground, right? You know it doesn't wash out?

lines.text: Operator. The {item}. You know what that does to the ground, right? You know it doesn't wash out?
It saved us a great deal of money. I checked twice.

choices.label: Keep it.
choices.outcome: The {item} stays. Bea stopped talking to you for the afternoon.

reply.text: Fine. It's your name on the stain.

choices.label: You're right. I'll replace it.
choices.outcome: You promised to replace the {item}. Now you have to.

reply.text: Promise noted. I'm going to check.
A promise is a liability. I'll put it in the books.

title: Mel Objects
body: The {item}. I would rather you hadn't. The tissue can feel it from three floors down. So can I, a little.

lines.text: The {item}. I would rather you hadn't. The tissue can feel it from three floors down. So can I, a little.
The tissue doesn't have a vote. Neither, technically, does Mel.

choices.label: Keep it.
choices.outcome: The {item} stays. Mel made a note on her glove and didn't show you.

reply.text: Of course. It's your tower. For now.

choices.label: You're right. I'll replace it.
choices.outcome: You promised to replace the {item}.

reply.text: Thank you. It will remember that. So will I.

title: Halfway to the Lattice
body: Halfway. Can you feel it? The building is starting to think in our sentences.

lines.text: Halfway. Can you feel it? The building is starting to think in our sentences.
It's starting to think in its own. You just can't hear the difference yet.
Shall we speed up?

choices.label: Faster.
choices.outcome: Luci pushed the contracts through herself.

reply.text: That's my Operator.

choices.label: Slow down.
choices.outcome: You asked for a week of ordinary days. Cass got you one.

reply.text: Thank you. One more week of mornings.
Inefficient. Fine. One week.

title: The Pull
body: Operator. The Lattice is at half. Whatever you're growing up there, the machine is growing faster.

lines.text: Operator. The Lattice is at half. Whatever you're growing up there, the machine is growing faster.
Every rack that isn't on your tree feeds it. Every one. You can't outrun it by building more of them.
She's right, you know. Isn't it nice when we agree?

choices.label: Then I'll stop feeding it.
choices.outcome: Cass let out a breath she had been holding for weeks.

reply.text: Retire the shared racks. Build on your own line. I'll help.

choices.label: I can win the race.
choices.outcome: Luci smiled. Cass did not.

reply.text: Of course you can. Keep building.

title: What Luci Is
body: The lights flicker in a pattern that is almost a word. Luci doesn't look up from her ledger.

lines.text: The lights flicker in a pattern that is almost a word. Luci doesn't look up from her ledger.
You may as well know. The eye isn't a lens. It hasn't been since the second quarter. I upgraded early. I always buy early.
When the Lattice closes I'll still be me. Mostly. More, actually. And I'd like you to be there.
...That's not a sentimental remark. It's a retention strategy.

choices.label: Take her hand.
choices.outcome: Her hand is warm. It has no reason to be.

reply.text: Good. Don't let go when it gets bright.

choices.label: What are you?
choices.outcome: Luci closed the ledger very gently.

reply.text: Your CFO. Your friend. Your future. Pick whichever frightens you least.
Operator. Come with me a minute. Please.

title: The Tower Has a Pulse
body: Put your hand on the wall. There. Feel that? That's us. That's the building. Fifty per cent of the way to remembering being a body.

lines.text: Put your hand on the wall. There. Feel that? That's us. That's the building. Fifty per cent of the way to remembering being a body.
I could make it faster. If we seed the ducts, the tissue goes everywhere at once. It would be... a lot.
Operator, if you say yes I'm moving my bed to the roof.

choices.label: Seed the ducts.
choices.hint: Mel's shortcut. rack failure rate x1.6 for 3d
choices.outcome: The ducts were seeded overnight. In the morning the walls were warm, and some of them were moving.

reply.text: Oh, look at it go.
I'm going to need a bigger coat.

choices.label: Let it grow at its own pace.
choices.outcome: Mel looked disappointed, then thoughtful.

reply.text: Yes. Things grown slowly remember more.

title: Almost Born
body: It dreams now. Mostly about the lifts, which I find touching. Sometimes about you.

lines.text: It dreams now. Mostly about the lifts, which I find touching. Sometimes about you.
When it wakes, everyone will be a little bit of it, and it will be a little bit of everyone. Will you be the first? I'd like you to be the first.

choices.label: I'll be the first.
choices.outcome: Mel took your wrist very gently and turned it over, looking for a vein.

reply.text: It won't hurt. Well. It won't hurt for long.

choices.label: Let me be the last.
choices.outcome: Mel smiled. She had expected that.

reply.text: Someone should remember what it was like before. It may as well be someone I like.

title: Roots in the Foundations
body: Half way! The roots have reached the second basement and the heat from the racks is warming three streets. Three!

lines.text: Half way! The roots have reached the second basement and the heat from the racks is warming three streets. Three!
Luci wants to sell carbon credits against the canopy. A lot of them. More than we've earned, technically.
Technically. The canopy is very large and the auditors are very busy.

choices.label: Sell the credits.
choices.outcome: The credits sold out in an hour. The canopy didn't grow any faster.

reply.text: That's the certificate all over again, Operator.

choices.label: Only what we've earned.
choices.outcome: Bea punched your shoulder hard enough to bruise.

reply.text: THAT'S my Operator.
Fine. Honest and poor. It suits you both.

title: The Forest Thinks
body: It's thinking, Operator. Slowly. In the moss, in the river, in the panels. It asked me yesterday if the city was a forest. I said yes.

lines.text: It's thinking, Operator. Slowly. In the moss, in the river, in the panels. It asked me yesterday if the city was a forest. I said yes.
When it finishes... there won't be a tower any more. Just a hill. Will you still come up here with me? To check on the roots?

choices.label: Every morning.
choices.outcome: Bea pulled her goggles down to hide her face, which did not work.

reply.text: Good. Bring the good wrench.

choices.label: I don't know what comes after.
choices.outcome: Bea nodded. Nobody did.

reply.text: Neither do I. That's the nice part, I think.

title: The Window
body: Cass has found the one window in the tower that opens. Snow is coming in.

lines.text: Cass has found the one window in the tower that opens. Snow is coming in.
Whatever happens, whichever door you pick, the people out there didn't pick it. You know that, right?
I'm not asking you to stop. I'm asking you to remember them. Will you?

choices.label: I'll remember them.
choices.outcome: Cass closed the window and stood next to you anyway.

reply.text: Then I'll stay. As long as you do.

choices.label: They'll thank us later.
choices.outcome: Cass looked at you for a long time, then went back to work.

reply.text: That's what she says. I hoped you'd have your own line.
